Line 54 is round 2's own proof row 6, whose negativeControl field quotes the fabricated MagicDNS host it wrote into a scratch file, spelled as an ordinary tailnet name rather than under the reserved placeholder. The check cannot tell a fabricated tailnet name from a real one, which is why the rule asks for the placeholder, so it refuses -- and the name is now in this public branch's history, the same shape as the incident at dispatch://INFRA-416. Control, run to show that this one field is the whole of the failure: with that field reworded to name the host instead of quoting it and nothing else touched, the check exits 0 over the same 6224 files; docs/kubernetes.md and .legion/INFRA-228/implement.json were restored afterwards and jj diff --stat is empty. The pull request's own text is clean: check-pr-text's rule finds no host in the title, the body or any comment, and this handoff and the tester's evidence comment were both scanned through check-private-names before they were written and posted. Why CI has not reported it: c718788b, the code head the CI router workflow is running on, predates that file, so its lint will pass, and 4d4f19d1 carries the skip-checks: true trailer, so nothing runs on it; the next push that is not handoff-only -- the reviewer's own prose-fix commit is one -- runs lint over a tree that carries the line and turns that required check red. No red test is needed: check-private-names is that test, and it is already red. Fix: reword .legion/INFRA-228/implement.json line 54 so it names the host rather than quoting it, or use example-tailnet.ts.net.
